items.title: Checkpointless training on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod: Production-scale training with faster fault recovery
items.raw_excerpt: In this post, we introduce checkpointless training on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod, a paradigm shift in model training that reduces the need for traditional checkpointing by enabling peer-to-peer state recovery. Results from production-scale validation show 80–93% reduction in recovery time (from 15–30 minutes or more to under 2 minutes) and enables up to 95% training goodput on cluster sizes with thousands of AI accelerators.

title_i18n.en: Checkpointless training on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod: Production-scale training with faster fault recovery
title_i18n.zh: 在Amazon SageMaker HyperPod上进行无检查点训练：实现生产规模训练与更快的故障恢复
title_i18n.es: Entrenamiento sin puntos de control en Amazon SageMaker HyperPod: Formación a escala de producción con recuperación de fallos más rápida

excerpt_i18n.en: In this post, we introduce checkpointless training on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod, a paradigm shift in model training that reduces the need for traditional checkpointing by enabling peer-to-peer state recovery. Results from production-scale validation show 80–93% reduction in recovery time (from 15–30 minutes or more to under 2 minutes) and enables up to 95% training goodput on cluster sizes with thousands of AI accelerators.
excerpt_i18n.zh: 在这篇文章中，我们介绍亚马逊SageMaker HyperPod的无检查点训练，这是一种模型训练范式的转变，通过启用点对点技术，减少了对传统检查点的需求。
excerpt_i18n.es: En esta publicación, presentamos el entrenamiento sin puntos de control en Amazon SageMaker HyperPod, un cambio de paradigma en el entrenamiento de modelos que reduce la necesidad de los puntos de control tradicionales al permitir la comunicación entre pares.

items.title: Tickerterm – AI-native algo trading platform
items.raw_excerpt: Hey HN, My co-founder and I built Tickerterm – making algo trading accessible through AI. We met at Bubble (employees #2 and #4). Watched AI coding change who could build software. excerpt_i18n.en: On a sunny Saturday at the base of Noitom Robotics, we met Dr. Dai Ruoli—co-founder of Noitom, and now also founder/CEO of Noitom Robotics—who combines technical acumen with entrepreneurial boldness. Recalling the origins of Noitom over a decade ago, Dr. Dai can still effortlessly cite the product code of the first iPhone gyroscope chip: L3G4200D. It was this tiny chip that alerted him to an opportunity, leading to the founding of Noitom. From film special effects to VR interaction and digital healthcare, Noitom has made its mark across multiple fields. And as the wave of robotics surged, he keenly recognized the potential of robotics data. "In 2024, robotics revenue for Noitom increased fivefold, and it grew again in 2025, ultimately rising 40 times over two years. As a business leader, you can’t ignore that!" Dr. Dai said with a smile. So, early this year, he decisively spun off the robotics business to establish a robotics data company. Speaking of this choice, he affirmed, "I am the most suitable person to run a robotics data company, and Noitom Robotics is the only company in the industry that truly understands how to handle this data business!" Notably, Dr. Dai attended the data session of the 2025 GAIR Global AI and Robotics Conference, delivering a presentation titled "Using Motion Capture...
excerpt_i18n.es: El sábado, bajo el edificio de Noitom Robotics, con el sol brillando en el suelo, nos encontramos con el Dr. Dai Ruoli, cofundador de Noitom, quien ahora también ostenta el título de fundador y CEO de Noitom Robotics. En él se combina la perspicacia tecnológica con la determinación de un emprendedor. Al recordar los orígenes de Noitom hace más de una década, Dai Ruoli aún puede mencionar de inmediato el código del primer chip giroscópico del iPhone: L3G4200D. Fue este pequeño chip lo que le hizo percibir una oportunidad y fundar Noitom. Desde efectos visuales cinematográficos, interacción en realidad virtual, hasta medicina digital, la huella de Noitom está presente en diversos campos.

items.title: Score Distillation of Flow Matching Models
items.raw_excerpt: Diffusion models achieve high-quality image generation but are limited by slow iterative sampling. Distillation methods alleviate this by enabling one- or few-step generation. Flow matching, originally introduced as a distinct framework, has since been shown to be theoretically equivalent to diffusion under Gaussian assumptions, raising the question of whether distillation techniques such as score distillation transfer directly. We provide a simple derivation — based on Bayes’ rule and conditional expectations — that unifies Gaussian diffusion and flow matching without relying on ODE/SDE…
